author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: I am not moving the deployment gate forward until we have a named owner for the risk assessment hand off. The pipeline can run, but I will not approve the release if that document lacks a formal signature. This is not a preference for extra paperwork. It is a hard stop. If the consent validation logic changes, the risk profile changes, and I need a specific person to take responsibility for that shift. Without that sign off, the service stays in staging. I will not take the blame for a production incident because the ownership was vague during the transition. Get me the name of the person who owns that assessment, and I will proceed. Until then, the gate remains closed.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a hard stop and refusal to approve the release without a named owner, establishing a non-negotiable line that must be met to proceed.
